books.title: Fog
books.art_why: Fog is a real weather condition that can be photographed today.

pages.text: Fog looks like low clouds.
pages.brief: A soft outdoor view shows fog hanging low in the air beside higher clouds, so the fog and clouds look alike. The fog spreads in a pale layer while the clouds sit above, making the two look very similar.

pages.text: Fog looks white and spooky.
pages.brief: A thick white fog fills the outdoor scene, pale and eerie. The fog drifts in a soft, spooky way, with no clear edges, so the whole view feels quiet, strange and unsettling.

pages.text: Fog can form out of small water drops.
pages.brief: A close view shows fog made from many small water drops floating together in the air. The tiny drops gather and drift as a soft mist, showing how fog can form out of small water drops.

pages.text: Fog can form out of tiny pieces of ice.
pages.brief: A close view shows fog made from tiny pieces of ice floating in the air. The little ice bits drift together in a cold mist, showing how fog can form out of tiny pieces of ice.

pages.text: Fog sometimes forms near water.
pages.brief: An outdoor scene shows pale fog drifting near a body of water. The fog hangs close to the water and spreads softly through the air, showing that fog sometimes forms near water.

pages.text: Fog sometimes forms near mountains.
pages.brief: An outdoor scene shows fog drifting near mountains. Pale fog hangs around the mountain slopes and spreads through the air, showing that fog sometimes forms near mountains. The mountain shapes rise behind the soft fog.

pages.text: Fog sometimes forms over wet land.
pages.brief: An outdoor view shows fog spreading over wet land. Pale fog drifts low over the damp ground, showing that fog sometimes forms over wet land. The wet land lies beneath the soft fog as it spreads across the scene.

pages.text: Fog always forms near the ground.
pages.brief: An outdoor scene shows fog lying low near the ground. The pale fog spreads close to the ground across the view, showing that fog always forms near the ground. The fog stays low in the outdoor scene.

pages.text: Fog always forms where air is still.
pages.brief: An outdoor scene shows fog in still air. The pale fog hangs in a quiet, motionless view, showing that fog always forms where air is still. The fog stays settled and smooth, with the air around it calm.

pages.text: Fog always makes it hard to see.
pages.brief: An outdoor view is filled with thick fog that makes seeing hard. The pale fog covers the scene so it is hard to see, showing that fog always makes it hard to see. The fog spreads across the whole view.

books.title: Insect Wings
books.art_why: All the insects are real animals that can be photographed today.

pages.text: Insects have many kinds of wings.
pages.brief: A close view of several different insects resting together on green leaves in a sunny garden, each one showing a different kind of wing — long, round, spotted, striped, clear and brightly colored — held out beside each other so the many shapes can be compared.

pages.text: Insects use their wings to fly.
pages.brief: Several insects lift off and fly above a meadow of tall grass and small flowers, wings spread wide and blurred with motion as they climb into the air, some flying low and some higher, with sunlight behind them.

pages.text: This wasp has blue wings.
pages.brief: A wasp grips a thin green stem in a garden, its wings glowing deep blue in the sunlight, folded back along its striped body while its legs hold tight to the plant and its antennae reach forward.

pages.text: This grasshopper has green wings.
pages.brief: A grasshopper sits on a blade of grass in a field, its green wings folded along its sides and blending with the stems around it, long back legs bent and ready to jump.

pages.text: This moth has spotted wings.
pages.brief: A moth rests on a rough tree trunk, its wings spread flat and covered in spots, the round marks standing out against the pale wing surfaces while its feathery antennae lie back.

pages.text: This dragonfly has striped wings.
pages.brief: A dragonfly perches on the tip of a twig beside a pond, its four wings held out flat and marked with stripes, its large eyes and long slender body facing the camera.

pages.text: This ant has clear wings.
pages.brief: An ant stands on a green leaf, its clear see-through wings raised above its body and catching the light, thin veins faintly visible while its legs grip the leaf surface.

pages.text: This butterfly has colorful wings.
pages.brief: A butterfly rests on a bright flower in a garden, its colorful wings spread open to show the pattern of shades across both sides while it holds the petals with its legs.

pages.text: Some insects have wing covers.
pages.brief: An insect clings to a tree trunk with hard wing covers closed over its back like a shell, hiding the flying wings underneath, the smooth covers catching the daylight as it walks upward.

pages.text: Insects have many kinds of wings.
pages.brief: Another close view of several insects gathered on leaves and stems in a sunny garden, each showing a different kind of wing — spotted, striped, clear, green, blue and colorful — spread out for comparison.

books.title: Imagine the Beach
books.art_why: Real beaches, waves, birds, sand and ice cream exist and can be photographed.

pages.text: Close your eyes.
pages.brief: A young child sits quietly with eyes gently closed, face calm and relaxed, ready to imagine. The setting is simple and soft, with no distractions, focusing only on the child’s peaceful expression and the instruction to shut out the world and begin imagining.

pages.text: Can you imagine the beach in your mind?
pages.brief: The child, eyes still closed, imagines a beach in their mind. A sandy shore and calm ocean appear in their imagination, with soft light, showing the child picturing the beach clearly before exploring it with their senses.

pages.text: What can you smell? Can you smell the salty air?
pages.brief: At the imagined beach, a child stands near the water and breathes in deeply through the nose. Salty sea air drifts around them from the ocean, and the child’s calm face shows they are noticing the smell of the beach.

pages.text: What can you hear? Can you hear the crashing waves?
pages.brief: A child on the beach turns an ear toward the ocean, listening. Large waves roll in and crash onto the shore, sending white foam across the sand. The child’s expression is attentive, showing they can hear the crashing waves clearly.

pages.text: What can you see? Can you see the diving birds?
pages.brief: A child looks up at the beach sky as seabirds dive toward the water. The birds fold their wings and plunge down, while the child watches with wide eyes, noticing the diving birds above the waves and the open air.

pages.text: What can you feel? Can you feel the rough sand?
pages.brief: A child kneels on the beach and presses both hands into the sand. The sand looks coarse and grainy, and the child’s fingers spread through it, showing the rough texture. The child concentrates on the feeling under their hands.

pages.text: What can you taste? Can you taste the yummy ice cream?
pages.brief: A child at the beach holds a cone of ice cream and takes a happy bite. The ice cream looks cool and sweet, and the child’s pleased face shows the yummy taste. Sand and ocean are nearby in the background.

pages.text: What else can you imagine at the beach? What do your mind and senses tell you?
pages.brief: A child stands on the beach with a thoughtful, wondering expression, looking out at the shore. Their face shows they are using their mind and senses to imagine more at the beach, with open sky and calm surroundings inviting further ideas.

books.title: River Otters
books.art_why: Real river otters and their watery habitat can be photographed.

pages.text: River otters are amazing animals.
pages.brief: A river otter stands at the edge of a river, its sleek body raised as it looks out over the water. The otter appears alert and lively, showing how amazing this animal is in its natural riverside setting.

pages.text: All river otters live near water.
pages.brief: A river otter swims in a river, its head above the surface, with open water around it. The otter stays close to the river as it moves, showing that river otters live near water at all times.

pages.text: All river otters have long, thin bodies.
pages.brief: A river otter stretches out beside the water, showing its long, thin body from head to tail. Its body looks smooth and slender as it lies near the river, matching the shape of every river otter.

pages.text: All river otters have short legs.
pages.brief: A river otter stands on a riverbank, its long body held low on its short legs. The short legs are clearly visible as the otter moves along the edge of the water in its riverside home.

pages.text: All river otters have thick, warm fur.
pages.brief: A river otter sits near the water with its thick, warm fur clearly visible over its body. The fur looks dense and soft as the otter rests by the river, keeping the animal warm in its natural setting.

pages.text: All river otters are good at swimming.
pages.brief: A river otter swims strongly through the river, its body moving smoothly through the water. Its head and back break the surface as it paddles forward with ease, showing how good river otters are at swimming.

pages.text: All river otters are good at holding their breath.
pages.brief: A river otter stays underwater with its mouth closed, holding its breath as it swims below the surface. The otter remains calm and steady in the river, showing how good river otters are at holding their breath.

pages.text: All river otters are good at catching food.
pages.brief: A river otter catches food in the river, reaching for it as it swims near the surface. The otter focuses on the food in the water, showing how good river otters are at catching food.

pages.text: All river otters are good at playing together.
pages.brief: Two river otters play together near the water, tumbling and moving around each other with energy. Their bodies look lively as they interact in the riverside setting, showing how good river otters are at playing together.

pages.text: River otters are special animals. All river otters are good at being river otters.
pages.brief: A river otter stands beside the river, looking alert and at home in its natural setting. The otter rests near the water with a calm, confident pose, showing that river otters are special animals good at being river otters.

books.title: Bubbles
books.art_why: Real bubbles, people and solid materials can all be photographed directly.

pages.text: Bubbles are round pockets of air inside a material. People make bubbles with many things.
pages.brief: A close view of a clear material with round pockets of air trapped inside it. Nearby, several people use different materials to make bubbles, each person holding or blowing into something that forms round bubbles in the air.

pages.text: People make bubbles with soap.
pages.brief: A child holds soapy water in cupped hands and blows gently, forming round soap bubbles that lift into the air. Another child nearby blows bubbles from a small wand. Sunlight shines on the wet, shiny bubbles.

pages.text: People make bubbles while chewing gum.
pages.brief: A boy chews gum and blows a large pink bubble from his mouth. The round bubble stretches wide in front of his face. He sits at a table, watching the gum bubble grow.

pages.text: People make bubbles in milk.
pages.brief: A glass of milk stands on a kitchen table, its surface covered with small round bubbles. A young girl leans close, watching the bubbles pop and reform. The white milk and clustered bubbles fill the frame.

pages.text: People make bubbles under water.
pages.brief: A swimmer is underwater in a pool, exhaling a stream of round bubbles from the mouth and nose. The silver bubbles rise toward the surface. Blue water surrounds the swimmer, and more bubbles trail upward in a bright column.

pages.text: Some bubbles are colorful.
pages.brief: Close-up of a single soap bubble floating in sunlight, its surface shining with swirls of pink, green, blue and gold. The thin, round film reflects light in colorful bands. A soft blurred background keeps attention on the bright bubble.

pages.text: Some bubbles stick together.
pages.brief: Several soap bubbles press together in a foamy cluster, their round shapes flattening where they touch. The joined bubbles form a mass of shiny, wet surfaces. Light reflects off each curved side, showing where the bubbles stick together.

pages.text: Some bubbles float away.
pages.brief: A few round bubbles drift upward and away across open air. They spread apart as they rise, carried by a light breeze. The bubbles grow smaller and smaller as they float off into the distance.

pages.text: Some bubbles are in solids.
pages.brief: A solid block of clear material is shown close up, with round air bubbles trapped inside it. The bubbles sit frozen in place within the solid. Light passes through the block, making the trapped round pockets visible throughout.

pages.text: Bubbles hold air. Some bubbles hold people, too!
pages.brief: A giant clear inflatable bubble rests on the ground, with people sitting inside it. The round bubble holds the people and the air around them. Outside, a few smaller bubbles float nearby, showing bubbles that hold only air.

books.title: Cranberries
books.art_why: Cranberries, bogs and vines are real plants that can be photographed today.

pages.text: Cranberries are fruits. They grow in bogs.
pages.brief: A wide view of a low, wet bog with shallow water and mossy ground, where small round red cranberries sit among the stems and leaves near the surface. Soft daylight and still water show the damp, marshy place where these fruits grow.

pages.text: Cranberries are fruits. They grow on vines.
pages.brief: A close view of thin cranberry vines creeping low across the ground, with small green leaves and a few firm red berries hanging among them. The trailing stems spread over the soil, showing the fruit growing on the plant rather than on a tree.

pages.text: Cranberries are fruits. They grow pink flowers.
pages.brief: A close-up of a cranberry vine in bloom, with several small pink flowers opening on slender stems above the green leaves. The petals are turned back and pointed, and the tiny flowers sit close to the low-growing plant in soft natural light.

pages.text: Cranberries are fruits. They grow slowly.
pages.brief: A quiet view of a cranberry vine spreading slowly over damp ground, with small green berries and a few ripening red ones at different stages along the stems. Low light and a wide patch of ground suggest slow, gradual growth over time.

pages.text: Cranberries taste tart. People eat them fresh.
pages.brief: A pair of hands holds a small handful of fresh, firm red cranberries, shiny and round, with a few loose berries resting nearby on a light wooden surface. The berries look bright and whole, ready to be eaten just as they are.

pages.text: Cranberries taste tart. People eat them dried.
pages.brief: A small bowl of dried cranberries, wrinkled and deep red, sits on a plain table with a few dried pieces scattered beside it. A hand reaches in to take some, showing the chewy dried fruit being eaten as a snack.

pages.text: Cranberries taste tart. People eat them as jam.
pages.brief: A glass jar of dark red cranberry jam stands open on a kitchen table beside a spoon and a slice of bread spread with the jam. The thick, glossy jam shows how the tart fruit is cooked down and eaten.

pages.text: Cranberries taste tart. People eat them as sauce.
pages.brief: A small jug pours smooth dark red cranberry sauce into a dish on a table, with a spoon resting alongside. The shiny sauce sits ready to be served and eaten with a meal, showing another way people enjoy the tart fruit.

books.title: Reindeer Are Real
books.art_why: Reindeer are real animals living today, so real photographs fit.

pages.text: Did you know that reindeer are real? Well, they are.
pages.brief: A single reindeer stands on open snowy tundra, its breath misting in the cold air. It faces forward with antlers held high, thick coat ruffled by the wind. Pale winter light falls over low hills and scattered snow-covered shrubs behind it.

pages.text: Reindeer sometimes pull sleds.
pages.brief: A reindeer harnessed to a wooden sled moves across packed snow, head lowered as it pulls. The sled runners cut fresh tracks behind it. Snow-covered ground and bare winter trees stretch around the scene in cold light.

pages.text: Reindeer sometimes dig for food.
pages.brief: A reindeer stands in deep snow, one front hoof scraping and digging down through the white crust. Its muzzle dips toward the hollow it has made, searching for food beneath. Snow clumps on its legs and antlers.

pages.text: Reindeer sometimes weigh a lot.
pages.brief: A large reindeer stands broadside on a snowy slope, its heavy body and thick neck filling much of the view. Its coat looks dense and warm, legs planted firmly. Snow banks and low hills spread out around it.

pages.text: Reindeer sometimes swim.
pages.brief: A reindeer swims across a wide river, head and antlers above the water while its body stays half-submerged. Ripples spread from its chest as it pushes forward. Green banks and grey sky lie beyond the water.

pages.text: Reindeer sometimes travel many miles.
pages.brief: A line of reindeer moves across a vast open landscape, walking one behind another over tundra and low ridges. Their hooves beat a trail through the snow, and the herd stretches toward distant hills under a wide sky.

pages.text: All reindeer have thick fur.
pages.brief: A close view of a reindeer's thick coat, long hairs packed densely over its neck and shoulder. The fur looks shaggy and warm, with a lighter ruff around the throat. A blurred snowy background surrounds the animal.

pages.text: All reindeer eat only plants.
pages.brief: A reindeer bends its head to feed on low green plants, grasses and leafy shoots at the edge of a snow patch. Its muzzle touches the plants while it chews. More small plants push up through the thawing ground nearby.

pages.text: All reindeer can walk on ice.
pages.brief: A reindeer walks steadily across a sheet of smooth ice, hooves spread and gripping the slick surface. A faint reflection shows below, and snow dusts the edges of the frozen ground. Cold sky and bare land lie beyond.

pages.text: All reindeer can walk the day they are born.
pages.brief: A newborn reindeer calf stands on thin, wobbly legs on snowy ground, taking its first steps. Its small coat looks soft, and its hooves press into the snow. The calf moves forward, walking on the day it was born.

books.title: How Do They Swim?
books.art_why: All eight animals are real and can be photographed today.

pages.text: Fish can swim. They use their fins and tails to swim.
pages.brief: Several fish swimming underwater in a clear pond or river, bodies curved as they move, their fins spread out to the sides and their tails sweeping behind them, pushing them through the water past smooth stones and soft green water plants.

pages.text: Ducks can swim. They use their feet to swim.
pages.brief: A mother duck on a calm pond with her ducklings close behind, her orange webbed feet paddling just under the surface, ripples spreading out behind her as she glides forward past low green reeds at the water's edge.

pages.text: Beavers can swim. They use their feet and tails to swim.
pages.brief: A beaver swimming across a pond at dusk, its wide flat tail trailing behind and its strong back feet kicking underwater, ripples around its brown furry head as it heads toward a pile of sticks and mud on the bank.

pages.text: Turtles can swim. They use their feet or flippers to swim.
pages.brief: A sea turtle gliding through blue ocean water, its front flippers sweeping forward while its back flippers steer, and nearby a smaller freshwater turtle paddling in shallow green water with its feet on the muddy bottom.

pages.text: Otters can swim. They use their feet and tails to swim.
pages.brief: An otter swimming on its back in a river, dark wet fur sleek against the water, its strong tail and small webbed feet moving together to push it along, while another otter dives nearby among river stones.

pages.text: Bears can swim. They use their paws to swim.
pages.brief: A large brown bear wading and swimming across a wide river, its big paws paddling under the surface, water streaming off its shoulders and head held high as it crosses toward a grassy bank.

pages.text: Seals can swim. They use their flippers to swim.
pages.brief: A seal swimming in cold grey-blue sea water, its smooth spotted body rolling forward while its front flippers push and its back flippers trail like a rudder, its whiskered face near the surface.

pages.text: Snakes can swim. They use their bodies to swim.
pages.brief: A long green and brown snake swimming across the surface of a quiet pond, its body winding in smooth curves from side to side, head lifted slightly, leaving a rippling trail on the still water behind it.

books.title: Community Helpers
books.art_why: Community helpers are real people who can be photographed in everyday life.

pages.text: Who are the helpers in our community? Let us meet some of them.
pages.brief: A welcoming neighbourhood community scene shows a friendly group of community helpers standing together outdoors today, smiling and ready to be met. They are the helpers who serve the people around them in this community.

pages.text: This is a teacher. She is an important helper. She lives in our community.
pages.brief: A friendly woman teacher stands in the community today, smiling warmly at everyone. She is shown as an important helper who lives in this community, standing calmly and proudly as part of the neighbourhood around her.

pages.text: This is a trash collector. He is an important helper. He lives in our community.
pages.brief: A man trash collector stands in the community today, standing calmly in his work clothes. He is shown as an important helper who lives in this community, standing proudly as part of the neighbourhood around him.

pages.text: This is a baker. He is an important helper. He lives in our community.
pages.brief: A man baker stands in the community today, standing calmly in his baker clothes. He is shown as an important helper who lives in this community, standing proudly as part of the neighbourhood around him.

pages.text: This is a construction worker. She is an important helper. She lives in our community.
pages.brief: A woman construction worker stands in the community today, standing calmly in her work clothes. She is shown as an important helper who lives in this community, standing proudly as part of the neighbourhood around her.

pages.text: This is a firefighter. He is an important helper. He lives in our community.
pages.brief: A man firefighter stands in the community today, standing calmly in his firefighter clothes. He is shown as an important helper who lives in this community, standing proudly as part of the neighbourhood around him.

pages.text: This is a doctor. She is an important helper. She lives in our community.
pages.brief: A woman doctor stands in the community today, standing calmly in her doctor clothes. She is shown as an important helper who lives in this community, standing proudly as part of the neighbourhood around her.

pages.text: This is a service dog. She is an important helper, too.
pages.brief: A friendly service dog stands in the community today, calm and alert. She is shown as an important helper too, standing quietly and proudly with a gentle, helpful look as part of the neighbourhood around her.

books.title: Where Animals Live
books.art_why: All the animals and places exist today and can be photographed.

pages.text: Animals live in many different places. Some live above the ground. Some live in the ground. Some live on the ground. Some live in the water.
pages.brief: A wide outdoor view showing animals in different kinds of places at once: one high above the ground among tall plants, one down inside a hole in the earth, one standing on open ground, and one swimming in the water. Sky, soil and water are all visible in a calm natural scene.

pages.text: The monkey lives in the trees, too. This bird lives in the trees.
pages.brief: A tall leafy tree fills the picture. A monkey grips a branch with hands and feet, tail curling, looking out. On a higher branch a small bird perches with folded wings. Green leaves and branches surround them, showing the trees as their home.

pages.text: This frog lives in a pond. The turtle lives in a pond, too.
pages.brief: A still pond surrounded by green plants. A frog sits half in the water near the bank, eyes up and legs folded. Nearby a turtle rests in the shallow water with its shell above the surface and its head out. Gentle ripples spread around them.

pages.text: The woodchuck lives in a burrow, too. This prairie dog lives in a burrow.
pages.brief: Two burrows open in a grassy field. A woodchuck stands at one hole, body low, front paws on the dirt mound. At the other burrow a prairie dog sits upright on its hind legs, watching. Short grass and bare soil surround the entrances.

pages.text: These bats live in a cave. This bear lives in a cave, too.
pages.brief: Inside a dim rocky cave, several bats hang upside down from the ceiling with wings folded close. Deeper in the cave a bear stands on the rocky floor, head lifted toward the bats. Rough stone walls and shadowy darkness surround them.

pages.text: The fox lives in the woods, too. This deer lives in the woods.
pages.brief: A woodland scene with tall trees and undergrowth. A fox stands on the leafy ground, ears up, bushy tail behind it. A little farther off a deer stands among the trunks, head turned. Brown leaves, ferns and shadows fill the woods around them.

pages.text: This octopus lives in the ocean. The whale lives in the ocean, too.
pages.brief: Under the ocean, blue water all around. An octopus floats with its arms spread wide. A whale swims nearby, large body and tail moving through the water. Soft light filters down from above, and the open sea stretches away behind them.

pages.text: People are animals, too. Mandy and Michael live in a house.
pages.brief: A house with a garden. Mandy, a young girl, and Michael, a young boy, stand together by the front door. The house has windows and a roof behind them. They are at home, people who are animals too, living in a house.

books.title: The Team
books.art_why: Baseball teams and players exist in the real world today.

pages.text: Teams have players. A baseball team has nine players. Each player is important.
pages.brief: A baseball team of nine players in matching uniforms stands together on a grass field. They are gathered as a group, showing that every player on the team has a place and is important.

pages.text: She pitches the ball to the batter. The pitcher is very important.
pages.brief: A pitcher stands on the pitcher's mound and throws the baseball toward a batter waiting at home plate. The pitcher's arm is extended forward as the ball leaves the hand, showing the pitch in motion.

pages.text: The batter is very important. He hits the ball the pitcher pitches.
pages.brief: A batter stands at home plate, gripping a bat and swinging at the baseball coming from the pitcher. The bat meets the ball in front of the batter, and the batter's body twists with the hit.

pages.text: He catches the ball The catcher is very important. the pitcher pitches.
pages.brief: A catcher crouches behind home plate in protective gear, reaching up with a mitt to catch the baseball thrown by the pitcher. The catcher stays low, eyes on the pitch, ready to hold the ball securely.

pages.text: The infielder is very important. She catches the ball the batter hits.
pages.brief: An infielder stands on the dirt part of the baseball field, glove ready, and catches the baseball after the batter hits it. The infielder bends and reaches for the ball, keeping it in the glove.

pages.text: He catches the ball the batter hits. The outfielder is very important.
pages.brief: An outfielder stands in the grassy outfield, glove raised, and catches the baseball that the batter hit. The player is far from the infield, with open grass around, and holds the ball after the catch.

pages.text: All the players are important. To win, a team needs each player.
pages.brief: All the baseball players gather together on the field, pitcher, batter, catcher, infielder, and outfielder included. Some hold gloves; others stand close, united as a group, showing every player is needed to win.

pages.text: Players play together to win. Baseball is a team sport.
pages.brief: The baseball players play together on the field, moving as a team during the game. They work with one another, pitcher, batter, catcher and fielders, showing that baseball is a team sport played to win.

books.title: Clouds
books.art_why: Clouds, sky shapes, and rain are real-world nature subjects that can be photographed.

pages.text: Big white clouds fill the blue sky. What do you see in the clouds?
pages.brief: A wide blue sky filled with large, billowing white clouds. The clouds are bright and soft-edged, taking up most of the view, with clear blue spaces between them. No other objects or people are visible.

pages.text: What do you see? I see a snowman. Look at the puffy clouds.
pages.brief: Puffy white clouds gather into a snowman shape: a round body, a smaller head, and a suggestion of a hat, all formed from cloud. The surrounding sky is blue. The snowman shape is the clear focus among the soft cloud edges.

pages.text: Look at the jumbo clouds. A whale is what I see. What do you see?
pages.brief: Huge, jumbo white clouds fill the sky. Their rounded mass forms the shape of a whale, with a broad body and a tail-like edge. Blue sky shows around the cloud whale. The clouds look thick and towering.

pages.text: What do you see? I see a creamy pie. Look at the round clouds.
pages.brief: Round white clouds cluster in a blue sky, their soft edges forming a creamy pie shape. The pie-cloud has a rounded top and a wide base, like a pie with a crust. The clouds look smooth and bright.

pages.text: Do you see the fuzzy clouds? A sheep is what I see. Do you see it, too?
pages.brief: Fuzzy white clouds spread across the blue sky. Their soft, woolly shapes form a sheep: a fluffy body and a small head. The cloud sheep stands out against the blue, with wispy edges making it look fuzzy.

pages.text: Can you see the mountain? I see a mountain. Look at the very tall clouds.
pages.brief: Very tall white clouds rise high in the blue sky. Their steep, pointed shapes form a mountain, with a peak and sloping sides. The cloud mountain looks huge and towering, with clear sky around it.

pages.text: Look at the darker clouds. I see a thick blanket. What do you see?
pages.brief: Darker grey clouds fill the sky, thick and heavy. Their wide, layered shapes look like a thick blanket stretched across the sky. The clouds are dense and low, with little blue sky showing.

pages.text: Let’s go inside. It’s starting to rain.
pages.brief: Dark grey clouds release the first raindrops. Rain begins to fall in thin streaks from the heavy clouds. The sky is gloomy, and the ground below looks wet. The scene shows the start of rain.

books.title: Senses
books.art_why: A child's garden, birds, bees, flowers and a caterpillar are all real and can be photographed today.

pages.text: I like to learn about things. How do I learn about things? I use my five senses.
pages.brief: A young child stands in a sunny garden with green plants around, looking curious and thoughtful, head slightly tilted, one hand raised as if wondering. The child is the only person shown, simply standing and thinking about the world, with soft daylight and open space behind.

pages.text: I see birds and bees. I use my eyes to see.
pages.brief: The same young child crouches low in a garden and watches closely. A small bird perches nearby and a bee hovers over blossoms. The child's eyes are wide and focused on the bird and the bee, both clearly visible in front of the child among leaves and flowers.

pages.text: I use my ears to hear. I hear birds singing. I hear bees buzzing.
pages.brief: The child sits still in the garden, head turned and listening. A bird sings from a branch above, beak open, and a bee buzzes close to a flower. The child's calm face and attentive pose show the child hearing both sounds in the quiet garden.

pages.text: I smell pretty flowers. I use my nose to smell.
pages.brief: The child leans in toward a cluster of bright pretty flowers and sniffs them, nose close to the petals, eyes half closed and happy. Green stems and leaves surround the blossoms, and the child's hands rest gently near the flowers in the garden.

pages.text: I use my fingers to touch. I touch the fuzzy caterpillar.
pages.brief: The child's fingers reach out and lightly touch a fuzzy caterpillar crawling on a green leaf. The close view shows the caterpillar's soft bristly body and the child's careful fingertips, with garden leaves and stems filling the space around them.

pages.text: I taste sweet berries. I use my tongue to taste.
pages.brief: The child holds a handful of small sweet berries and tastes one, lips touching the fruit, with a pleased expression. The berries sit in the child's palm, and garden plants and sunlight fill the background behind the child's hands and face.

pages.text: I like to go to my garden. I use my five senses. I use them to see and hear.
pages.brief: The child stands happily in the middle of a lush garden, surrounded by flowers and greenery. A bird sings on a branch and a bee moves between blossoms. The child looks around with a bright, wide-awake face, taking in the sights and sounds of the garden.

pages.text: I learn a lot from my senses. I use them to touch. I use them to smell and taste.
pages.brief: The child sits in the garden, content and full of discovery, touching a leaf with the fingertips while flowers bloom close by and berries rest nearby. The child's face shows quiet satisfaction, with green plants, sunlight and open garden space all around.

books.title: Caretakers
books.art_why: Real people at work today — farmers, vets, doctors — are photographed, not drawn.

pages.text: Caretakers take care of things. There are many kinds of caretakers.
pages.brief: A group of different caretakers shown together in one wide scene, each one busy looking after something different — a clear, bright introduction to the many kinds of caretakers in the world around us.

pages.text: She takes care of farms. This farmer is a caretaker.
pages.brief: A woman farmer in work clothes stands out on her farm, tending the land she looks after. Wide view of the farm fields and buildings behind her, showing the place she takes care of every day.

pages.text: This babysitter is a caretaker. He takes care of children.
pages.brief: A man babysitter sits on the floor at home with young children, playing with them and keeping them safe. Toys nearby, warm indoor light, and the children close to him as he takes care of them.

pages.text: She takes care of the roads. This road worker is a caretaker.
pages.brief: A woman road worker in a high-visibility jacket and hard hat stands on a road, taking care of it. Road surface and markings in view, with her tools and equipment beside her as she works.

pages.text: This vet is a caretaker. He takes care of animals.
pages.brief: A man vet in a clinic gently holds and examines an animal, taking care of it. Clean examination room around him, his hands steady on the animal as he checks it over.

pages.text: She takes care of people. This doctor is a caretaker.
pages.brief: A woman doctor in a white coat stands with people she is looking after, talking with them calmly. Bright, clean medical setting around her as she takes care of her patients.

pages.text: This dentist is a caretaker. He takes care of teeth.
pages.brief: A man dentist in a dental clinic takes care of teeth, leaning in to check a patient's mouth. Dental chair, lamp and tools in the room around him as he works carefully.

pages.text: They take care of people, too. teachers are caretakers. These firefighters and.
pages.brief: Teachers in a classroom with children, and firefighters in gear standing together — caretakers who take care of people too. The two kinds of workers shown side by side as people who look after others.

books.title: Where Plants Grow
books.art_why: Plants and their habitats are real, so photographs fit.

pages.text: Plants grow in many places. They can grow outside. They can grow inside, too.
pages.brief: Green plants stand growing in an outdoor garden, and other leafy plants grow indoors in a bright room. The outdoor plants rise from the ground while the indoor plants sit in view, showing plants can grow in both places.

pages.text: Most plants grow in soil.
pages.brief: A wide view shows most plants growing in dark soil. Their green stems and leaves rise above the ground while their roots are hidden in the soil beneath them. The scene focuses on plants rooted in soil.

pages.text: Some plants grow in pots. There is soil inside the pots.
pages.brief: Several green plants grow in separate small pots. Each pot clearly holds soil inside, and the plants rise from that soil. The pots sit together in a simple setting, showing plants growing in soil-filled pots.

pages.text: Some plants grow in sand.
pages.brief: Small plants grow in pale sand. Their green stems and leaves stand above the sandy ground, with grains of sand around their bases. The view shows plants making a home in sand rather than soil.

pages.text: Some plants grow in water.
pages.brief: Several small green water plants grow in clear, steady water. Their leaves and stems rise through the water while roots spread below the surface. A full view shows plants living in water instead of soil.

pages.text: Some plants grow on rocks.
pages.brief: Plants grow on rough, bare rocks. Small sturdy green plants cling to the rock surface, with stems and leaves reaching upward. The rocky ground around them shows plants can grow where there is little soil.

pages.text: Some plants even grow on other plants.
pages.brief: One small green plant grows clearly on another leafy plant. The smaller plant rests on the larger plant’s stem or branch, with its leaves spread out. The scene shows plants can grow on other plants.

pages.text: They need water, air, and sunlight. Plants need three things to grow.
pages.brief: A plant is shown with water, air, and sunlight around it. Water drops fall near its roots, air moves around its leaves, and bright sunlight shines down. These are the three things plants need to grow.

books.title: Who Runs Faster?
books.art_why: Real animals and a child exist today, so photographs are possible.

pages.text: This is a tortoise. A squirrel can run faster than a tortoise.
pages.brief: A tortoise walks slowly on short grassy ground, its patterned shell low to the earth. Nearby, a squirrel dashes past with its tail streaming behind, clearly moving faster than the tortoise. Both animals are outdoors in a sunny park-like setting with grass and a few small plants.

pages.text: A girl can run faster than a squirrel. This is a squirrel.
pages.brief: A young girl in everyday clothes runs across open grass, arms swinging, hair moving. Ahead of her a squirrel races along the ground, tail up. The girl gains on the squirrel, running faster, as both move across the grass.

pages.text: This is a girl. A giraffe can run faster than a girl.
pages.brief: A young girl runs on open ground, and a tall giraffe strides nearby on long legs, neck reaching high. The giraffe covers ground faster than the girl, moving past her across a grassy outdoor area with a few trees in the distance.

pages.text: A zebra can run This is a giraffe. faster than a giraffe.
pages.brief: A zebra gallops across open grassland with its striped body and mane visible, moving quickly. A giraffe runs nearby, tall neck forward, but the zebra is pulling ahead, faster than the giraffe. Dry grass and scattered trees fill the background under daylight.

pages.text: This is a zebra. A lion can run faster than a zebra.
pages.brief: A zebra runs across grassland, stripes clear, legs stretched in motion. A lion runs close beside or behind it, powerful body low, gaining speed. The lion moves faster than the zebra, closing the distance across the open grassy plain.

pages.text: An antelope can run This is a lion. faster than a lion.
pages.brief: A lion runs through grassland, mane and long body in motion. An antelope sprints ahead on slender legs, leaping over the ground, faster than the lion. The antelope pulls away across the open plain with dry grass and distant trees.

pages.text: This is an antelope. A cheetah can run faster than an antelope.
pages.brief: An antelope runs fast across the plain, body stretched. A cheetah sprints beside or behind it, long body low, spotted coat, tail out for balance, moving faster than the antelope. The cheetah closes the gap across open grassland with dry grass and a low horizon.

pages.text: Nothing can run faster than a cheetah. This is a cheetah.
pages.brief: A cheetah runs at full speed across open grassland, long spotted body stretched low, tail trailing, legs extended. Nothing else is near it on the plain. Dry grass and a low, open horizon surround the cheetah as it sprints alone.

books.title: The Busy Pond
books.art_why: A real pond with real plants and animals can be photographed today.

pages.text: I see water when I go to the pond. I can see land all around the water.
pages.brief: A still pond of blue-green water seen from the grassy bank, with open land — low green grass and scattered bushes — stretching all around the water on every side. Soft daylight, calm surface, no people and no animals, just water and the land around it.

pages.text: I see cattails when I go to the pond. They are very tall.
pages.brief: Tall cattails standing in a cluster at the edge of the pond, their long narrow leaves rising straight up and their brown seed heads topping the stalks well above the water. Green grass and reeds around their base, quiet pond water behind them, soft daylight.

pages.text: I see lily pads when I go to the pond. They are very round.
pages.brief: Round lily pads floating flat on the calm pond surface, their circular green leaves spread across the water in a loose group, with a small gap of open water between them. Soft daylight on the pond, gentle ripples, no animals on the pads.

pages.text: I see frogs when I go to the pond. They sit on the lily pads.
pages.brief: Green frogs sitting on the floating lily pads in the middle of the pond, resting on the round leaves with their legs folded, some facing the camera, some turned sideways. Calm water between the pads, soft daylight, reeds in the background.

pages.text: I see turtles when I go to the pond. They sit on a log.
pages.brief: Several turtles sitting on a fallen log at the edge of the pond, their shells resting on the bark, heads lifted toward the sun, lined up along the wood. Water below the log, grass and reeds nearby, soft daylight on their shells.

pages.text: I see ducks when I go to the pond. They swim on the water.
pages.brief: Ducks swimming on the open water of the pond, gliding across the surface and leaving small V-shaped ripples behind them. Soft daylight on their feathers, calm blue-green water, low green banks and reeds in the background.

pages.text: I see fish when I go to the pond. They swim in the water.
pages.brief: Fish swimming in the clear pond water, their bodies and fins visible as they move below the surface among soft green underwater plants. Ripples and light patterns on the water above them, no other animals, calm and quiet.

pages.text: I see many things when I go to the pond. The pond is a busy place.
pages.brief: A wide view of the busy pond: tall cattails at the edge, round lily pads floating, frogs sitting on the pads, a turtle on a log, ducks swimming and fish below the surface. Green land all around the water, soft daylight over the whole scene.
